$ xref disp

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com

Instructions reading or writing struct fields: non-stack memory operands with these displacements.

Locates loads, stores, and lea field-pointer computations at exact byte displacements, optionally intersecting offsets or filtering by SIB scale/stride.

Usage

xref disp [OPTIONS] <VALUES>...

Arguments and options

Arguments

<VALUES>...
Field displacements (0x... hex or decimal).

Options

--write
Only instructions writing the memory operand.
--lea
Only lea instructions taking the field's address.
--all
Functions accessing all of the given displacements (an intersection), with per-function counts.
--stride <STRIDE>
Only accesses whose base or index register was computed with this array element stride.
--stack
Include stack displacements and fields relative to explicitly address-taken stack buffers.
--in <WITHIN>
Only inside the function containing this address.

Examples

All examples were recorded on public binaries; see Provenance.

Disp 0x20 --in 0x9ef60

Non-stack memory loads/stores at offset +0x20 inside function 0x9ef60..0x9f518.

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped disp 0x20 --in 0x9ef60
Output
0x9efb8  in 0x9ef60  mov r15, [rsi+0x20]
1 hits
stderr
xref: load 549.4µs, total 1.7ms

Disp 0x18 --lea --in 0x65e30

Only lea instructions taking a +0x18 field address (--lea), annotating the receiving callee (; -> 0x1610a0).

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped disp 0x18 --lea --in 0x65e30
Output
0x65e84  in 0x65e30  lea rcx, [r12+0x18]
0x65e9d  in 0x65e30  lea rcx, [rcx+0x18]  ; -> 0x1610a0
2 hits
stderr
xref: load 513.8µs, total 1.8ms

Disp 0x20 --stride 0x8 --in 0x6f910

Only +0x20 accesses whose base/index register uses array stride 0x8 (--stride 0x8).

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped disp 0x20 --stride 0x8 --in 0x6f910

Reading the output

  • One line per instruction that accesses memory at one of the displacements through a non-stack base register: address, containing function, instruction.
  • With several displacements and --all, only functions that use every one of them are listed; --write keeps stores, --lea keeps address computations, --stride N looks for array element strides.

Limits

  • A displacement is a number, not a type: unrelated structures that use the same offset match too. Narrow with --in FN or combine offsets with --all, or use layout on one function.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on xref.stripped = a stripped xref build (the binary of the home-page examples). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
